ransac_cylinder — 3D robust_fit op

• Data kinds: points × normals → primitive

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.ransac_cylinder(points, normals, thresh, iters=800, seed=0) (to call the implementation directly, import ransac_fit; ransac_fit.ransac_cylinder(points, normals, thresh, iters=800, seed=0); from the registry, ops3d.get("ransac_cylinder"))

Usage

Outlier-robust RANSAC cylinder fitting (point normals are required).

The normals of a cylinder surface are orthogonal to the axis, so the axis direction is estimated from the cross product of the normals of 2 points → all points are projected onto the plane orthogonal to the axis → a circle is fitted in that plane → the inliers with |projected distance - r| < thresh are maximised. On the final inliers the axis is re-estimated more robustly (smallest singular direction of the SVD of the normals = axis), and the projected circle is refitted by least squares. If there are no normals, estimate them on the caller side before passing them.

Args:

points: (N,3) point cloud.

normals: (N,3) (unit) normal of each point.

thresh: threshold on |projected distance-r| for counting as an inlier.

iters: number of RANSAC iterations.

seed: random seed (deterministic).

Returns:

(params, inlier_mask, info). params = {"axis": (3,) unit axis, "point": (3,) a point on the axis,

"radius": float}. info holds the inlier count n_inliers / ratio inlier_ratio / iters.
